item.title: Top civilian honour to Rudy Giuliani: Ex-NYC mayor to get Presidential Medal of Freedom; Trump hails him as 'great American patriot'
item.description: Donald Trump announced that Rudy Giuliani will receive the Presidential Medal of Freedom, praising him as a great mayor and patriot. The announcement follows Giuliani's hospitalisation after a car accident in New Hampshire, where he was aiding a woman. Despite injuries, including a fractured vertebra, Giuliani is expected to recover and resume his activities.

item.title: ‘Very good actor’: Woody Allen wants to direct Trump again; recalls 1998 crole in Celebrity
item.description: Woody Allen expressed his desire to direct Donald Trump again, reminiscing about their collaboration on the 1998 film 'Celebrity.' Allen praised Trump's professionalism and charisma on set, noting his surprise at Trump's foray into politics given his previous interests. Despite political differences, Allen believes he could still direct Trump effectively, even as president.

item.title: US ends visa interview waivers from Sept 2; Is India spared from toughest restrictions?
item.description: Starting September 2, 2025, the US State Department will require in-person interviews for nearly all non-immigrant visa applicants, ending many age-based exemptions and renewal waivers. This change affects students, professionals, and frequent travelers, potentially leading to longer wait times for appointments. Nationals from specific countries face immediate interview requirements, and stricter rescheduling policies will be enforced.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Random Musing: Why Peter Navarro evoked the Brahmin Bogeyman
item.description: But jokes and commentary aside, the Brahmin Bogeyman is a peculiar and very long-standing secular tradition of Indian politics and academia, which goes back to the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi. From an Ayn Rand socialist utopia in the North to a Stalinist one in the South, Brahmins have been an easy scarecrow politically. In America, it was an easy code to target high-achieving Indians, accusing them of caste oppression and complicity, with even attempts at state legislation to “eradicate caste,” which was ostensibly shut down by a powerful voice in the White House.

item.title: UAE selected to host World Kickboxing Championships: First time event takes place outside Europe
item.description: Abu Dhabi will host the World Kickboxing Championships for Masters and Seniors from 21–30 November 2025 at ADNEC, marking the tournament’s first edition outside Europe. Over 2,000 athletes from 150 nations will compete. The hosting deal between WAKO and the UAE Federation underscores the country’s growing stature as a global hub for combat sports.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Egypt: Four months after death, Ibrahim Shika’s family alleges organ theft
item.description: Four months after the death of former Zamalek player Ibrahim Shika, his family has filed a legal complaint alleging organ theft and medical negligence. Shika, who died at 28 after battling rectal cancer, is now at the center of an investigation. Authorities are examining claims that organs were removed post-mortem, with suspicions directed toward his widow.

item.title: 'Blatant interference by Russia': EU chief's plane hit by GPS jamming; lands safely in Bulgaria
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen's plane faced suspected Russian GPS jamming during landing in Bulgaria. Bulgarian authorities suspect Russian interference. The plane landed safely at Plovdiv International Airport. Von der Leyen was visiting Bulgaria as part of a tour. The region is vulnerable to "Russian hybrid threats."

item.title: US dollar holds steady against Egyptian pound across major banks on September 1
item.description: The US dollar exchange rate remained stable against the Egyptian pound on September 1, 2025, across all major Egyptian banks. The Central Bank of Egypt recorded EGP 48.52 for buying and EGP 48.66 for selling. Most banks, including NBE, Banque Misr, CIB, and others, posted consistent rates of EGP 48.54 for buying and EGP 48.64 for selling.

item.title: Flotilla with Greta Thunberg on board sets sail for Gaza
item.description: A flotilla carrying Greta Thunberg and humanitarian aid departed Barcelona for Gaza, aiming to break the maritime blockade. The convoy, with activists from 44 countries, seeks to deliver essential supplies. Thunberg criticized the world's silence on the deprivation in Gaza. This marks her second attempt to reach Gaza, amidst rising concerns over famine and potential US intervention plans.

item.title: South Australia bans fish-shaped soy sauce bottles leaving sushi lovers shocked; know why
item.description: South Australia has banned tiny, fish-shaped soy sauce bottles. These bottles pose environmental risks. They easily end up in waterways. The small size makes recycling difficult. This ban is part of a larger effort to reduce plastic waste. Other single-use plastics are also prohibited. The state aims to promote sustainable practices. Future bans are under consideration.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Asia Cup 2025: Match timings pushed back due to UAE heat, full revised schedule announced
item.description: The Asia Cup 2025, held in the UAE from September 9–28, will see revised match timings due to extreme heat, with 18 of 19 games now starting at 6:30 PM GST (8 PM IST). Featuring eight teams in a T20 format, the tournament includes high-profile clashes like India vs Pakistan and serves as key preparation for the ICC Champions Trophy.
